Dungeon World

Dungeon World is a tabletop RPG by Sage LaTorra and Adam Koebel that applies the Powered by the Apocalypse (PbtA) engine, originated by D. Vincent Baker’s Apocalypse World, to fantasy dungeon-crawling. Instead of a GM adjudicating a rules simulation, players and GM narrate the fiction first; when a character’s action fits a move’s trigger, the player rolls 2d6 and the result (10+, 7-9, 6-) determines the outcome in evocative, fiction-forward language. The GM never rolls dice — instead they make moves of their own, following an explicit agenda and set of principles.

Rules

Getting Started

  • Introduction — What Dungeon World is, per-class flavor, how to use the book, setting up a session
  • Playing the Game — Ability scores, making moves, harm and healing, magic, leveling up, bonds, alignment, hirelings
  • Basic Moves — Hack and Slash, Volley, Defy Danger, Defend, Spout Lore, Discern Realities, Parley, Aid or Interfere, with worked examples
  • Special Moves — Last Breath, Encumbrance, Make Camp, Take Watch, Undertake a Perilous Journey, End of Session, Level Up, Carouse, Supply, Recover, Recruit, Outstanding Warrants, Bolster
  • Character Creation — The 13-step process, ability score modifiers, worked example

Classes

  • Bard — Arcane Art, Bardic Lore, Charming and Open, A Port in the Storm
  • Cleric — Deity, Divine Guidance, Turn Undead, Commune, Cast a Spell, full spell list
  • Druid — Born of the Soil, Shapeshifter, Spirit Tongue, Studied Essence
  • Fighter — Bend Bars Lift Gates, Armored, Signature Weapon
  • Paladin — Lay on Hands, I Am the Law, Quest
  • Ranger — Hunt and Track, Called Shot, Animal Companion, Command
  • Thief — Trap Expert, Tricks of the Trade, Backstab, Poisoner
  • Wizard — Spellbook, Prepare Spells, Cast a Spell, Ritual, full spell list

Running the Game

  • The GM — Agenda, principles, GM moves, dungeon moves, dealing with common situations
  • Fronts — Dangers, grim portents, impending dooms, stakes, a worked example front
  • The World — Steadings, campaign maps, steading tags, making villages/towns/keeps/cities
  • First Session — Prep, getting started, the first adventure, GM goals
  • Example of Play — An annotated play transcript from a goblin ambush
  • Advanced Delving — Hacking the game: custom moves, new classes, compendium classes, adventure moves, monster hacking

Equipment

  • Equipment — Tags, weapons, armor, dungeon gear, poisons, services, magic items

Bestiary

  • Monsters — Monster tags, making monsters, treasure, the nine monster settings

Appendices

  • Adventure Conversion — Converting published adventures and other-system monsters to Dungeon World
  • Instant NPCs — 100 instincts, 100 knacks, and a name list for improvised NPCs

  • Character Sheet — Blank character sheet (printable) with interactive generator

Machine-Readable Data

Structured JSON, sourced from Sagelt/Dungeon-World (CC BY 3.0).

  • classes.json — Full class data: starting moves, advanced moves (2-5 and 6-10), races, alignments, bonds, gear, names
  • moves.json — 21 basic and special moves with triggers and outcomes
  • cavern-dwellers.json — Goblins, ankhegs, gargoyles, purple worms, and other cave and tunnel dwellers
  • lower-depths.json — Aboleths, dragons, minotaurs, nagas, and the deep-dwelling terrors of ancient ruins
  • twisted-experiments.json — Chimeras, golems, manticores, owlbears, and other creations of arcane hubris
  • folk-of-the-realm.json — Bandits, knights, nobles, spies, and the ordinary (and not-so-ordinary) people of the world
  • ravenous-hordes.json — Formians, gnolls, orcs, and tritons organized for war and conquest
  • planar-powers.json — Angels, devils, djinn, and the other creatures that slip through from beyond this world
  • swamp-denizens.json — Basilisks, hydras, lizardmen, trolls, and the rot and ruin of the fens
  • undead-legions.json — Ghosts, liches, vampires, zombies, and the many shapes death’s magic takes
  • dark-woods.json — Centaurs, dryads, treants, werewolves, and the sylvan monsters of the ancient forest
